elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: (1) Retrospective EHR extraction from 14 centers with demographics, time-stamped medication dosing, procedures, high-frequency nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes standardized to OMOP; (2) Waveform telemetry capture via gateway/middleware at each hospital in WFDB format (23TB); (3) Medical imaging acquisition from PACS in DICOM (7,642 admissions with radiology); (4) EEG recording extraction from hospital databases in EDF+/Persyst; collection_timeframes: September 1, 2022 through November 30, 2026, 14 hospitals, 45K+ admissions, target 100K+
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed collection mechanisms for all 4 data modalities with specific procedures, settings, and timeframes

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: (1) Structured EHR via OMOP transformation - demographics, time-stamped medication dosing, procedures, high-frequency nursing flowsheets, diagnoses (1.6B rows); (2) Clinical notes via OHNLP tokenization stored locally except tokens; (3) Medical imaging via DICOM from PACS with de-id in process; (4) Waveform telemetry via WFDB from bedside monitors through gateway/middleware (23TB); (5) EEG waveforms from hospital databases in EDF+/Persyst with extraction in process
sub_elements.quality_note: Five acquisition methods documented with specific instruments (PACS, bedside monitors, EHR systems), software (OMOP, OHNLP, WFDB), and data volumes

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, and Labeling Strategies
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: (1) OMOP CDM transformation with validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping repo, CHoRUSReports characterization; (2) Clinical note tokenization via OHNLP with full notes local, only tokens in enclave; (3) Waveform standardization to WFDB following extended PhysioNet schema (chorus_waveform repo); (4) Medical imaging DICOM de-id to remove PHI while preserving clinical utility (privacy_scan_tool); (5) Re-identification limitation transformations per HIPAA, geocoding via DeGauss; cleaning_strategies: multi-center harmonization with validated semantic mappings/SOPs, schema compliance validation across all modalities; labeling_strategies: visualization/annotation environment for prediction targets with clinical expert labeling and quality control per Chorus_SOP
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive preprocessing pipeline with 5 strategies, 2 cleaning approaches, and annotation environment with quality control

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.evidence: Tools mentioned: OMOP CDM, OHDSI tool stack, OHNLP toolkit, WFDB format, DICOM standard, EDF+ format, Persyst format, privacy_scan_tool, DeGauss (UF-Geocoding), Chorus_SOP protocols, CHoRUSReports, chorus-mapping repository, chorus_waveform repository, clinical validation SOP; GitHub organization with 28 repositories; visualization/annotation environment
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive software and tool documentation including standardization tools (OMOP, OHNLP, WFDB), privacy tools (privacy_scan_tool, DeGauss), and GitHub repositories

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: (1) Dataset actively growing - 45K admissions to 100K+ target, EEG extraction and full imaging de-id in process, clinical notes local storage with only tokens in enclave, cohort coverage varies by modality, ongoing collection through November 2026; (2) Controlled access restricts open research - DUA and institutional email required, secure enclave computational/logistical constraints
sub_elements.quality_note: Two major limitations explicitly documented with specific details on data completeness and access restrictions

sub_elements.name: Systematic Biases Identified and Described
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: (1) Academic medical center population bias - data from 14 acquisition centers across 20 academic institutions may not represent community hospital/rural care; patient populations at academic centers differ systematically in disease severity, demographics, treatment patterns; (2) Retrospective data collection bias - introduces selection biases based on documentation practices, coding patterns, clinical workflows varying across 14 centers; documentation completeness/accuracy varies by site, modality, time period
sub_elements.quality_note: Two systematic biases identified with detailed explanations of academic center bias and retrospective collection bias

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: missing_data_documentation: Incomplete modality coverage across sites - not all modalities available from all 14 centers, EEG extraction and full imaging de-id in process as of August 2025, clinical notes stored locally with only OHNLP tokens in central enclave, cohort coverage varies by modality during ongoing collection; known_limitations describe variation in documentation completeness/accuracy by site, modality, time period
sub_elements.quality_note: Quality issues documented including missing modality coverage and site-level variation in documentation

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: (1) Protected health information - complete EHR with demographics/diagnoses/procedures/medications/nursing documentation/clinical notes subject to HIPAA, de-identified before release through OMOP transformation and privacy scanning; (2) Physiological monitoring and EEG waveform data revealing sensitive health conditions/treatment responses in WFDB/EDF+/Persyst formats with controlled access; (3) Medical imaging in DICOM with de-id in process to remove embedded patient information; (4) Social Determinants of Health data including geographic information with privacy-preserving transformations
sub_elements.quality_note: Four categories of sensitive content documented with specific PHI types and protection mechanisms

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
